title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months of His Life. He's Becoming Parashurama.
excerpt: From wrapping Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War straight into Amar Kaushik's mythological epic Mahavatar — Kaushal's transformation into the immortal sage-warrior begins this month.
body:
There is a moment in every A-list actor's career where they stop calculating and start committing. For **Vicky Kaushal**, that moment is now.

The actor has blocked **18 consecutive months** — from June 2026 through December 2027 — exclusively for a single film: **Mahavatar**, Amar Kaushik's mythological epic about **Chiranjeevi Parashurama**, the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu. No side projects. No brand shoots squeezed in between schedules. No cameos in someone else's universe. Just one man, one god, and an eighteen-month window that might produce the most physically and emotionally demanding performance of his generation.

In an industry where top stars juggle three to four projects simultaneously, where release dates are announced before scripts are finished, this kind of devotion is either foolish or visionary. Knowing Kaushal's track record — **Chhaava**, **Uri**, **Sardar Udham** — it's almost certainly the latter.

## The Timeline

The preparation has already begun. Kaushal is currently wrapping his work on **Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War**, the lavish drama that reunites him with **Ranbir Kapoor** and **Alia Bhatt**. Bhansali is pushing to finish a crucial 50-day schedule that started in May, with the film targeting a January 21, 2027 theatrical release.

The moment Bhansali calls "cut" for the final time, Kaushal pivots immediately into what's being described as a "comprehensive six-month preparation module" designed by **Amar Kaushik** himself. This isn't a gym routine and a few dialect coaching sessions. According to reports, the program covers full physical transformation — Kaushal needs to build a wrestler's frame with long, matted hair and a rugged, almost feral appearance — alongside deep psychological and emotional workshops to inhabit a character who exists somewhere between mortal rage and divine purpose.

> "Vicky is treating Mahavatar as a once-in-a-lifetime project. He wants to be fully invested, which is why he has consciously decided not to take up any other assignments during the shoot." — Source close to the production

Principal photography begins **January 2027** and is expected to run an entire year, wrapping in December 2027. That's twelve months of continuous filming for a single project — a schedule that puts Mahavatar in the same logistical category as the Baahubali films and the upcoming Ramayana.

## Why Parashurama, and Why Now

**Amar Kaushik** has become one of the most commercially reliable directors in Indian cinema. The man behind **Stree**, **Bhediya**, and **Munjya** has built Maddock Films' horror-comedy universe into a billion-rupee franchise almost single-handedly. But Mahavatar represents something entirely different — a leap from genre entertainment into mythological world-building on a scale that Indian cinema has rarely attempted with this level of directorial pedigree.

Parashurama is a compelling choice. Unlike the more frequently adapted avatars — Ram, Krishna — Parashurama occupies a fascinating space in Indian mythology: a Brahmin warrior, furious and immortal, who wages war against corruption and injustice across generations. The character demands someone who can project both spiritual depth and terrifying physicality. After Chhaava, where Kaushal played Chhatrapati Sambhaji with a ferocity that earned him the best reviews of his career, he's proven he can occupy that space.

The first-look poster, which surfaced earlier this year, already set the internet on fire — a nearly unrecognisable Kaushal, matted locks, eyes burning, axe in hand. It was the kind of image that makes you stop scrolling.

## What It Means for Kaushal's Career

Here's the maths. By the time Mahavatar wraps in late 2027, Vicky Kaushal will have been essentially absent from the screen for over a year — save for Love and War's January release. That's a gamble. In Bollywood, out of sight has historically meant out of mind.

But Kaushal isn't building a career on volume anymore. He's building it on impact. **Uri** made him a star. **Sardar Udham** made him an actor. **Chhaava** made him a leading man. Mahavatar, if it works, makes him a legend.

Produced by **Dinesh Vijan** under the Maddock Films banner, Mahavatar is expected to release theatrically in 2028. Casting details beyond Kaushal remain under wraps, but given the scale, expect announcements in the coming months.

For diaspora audiences who've watched Kaushal evolve from the charming boy-next-door in Masaan to a man willing to disappear into roles that reshape his body and psyche — Mahavatar is the logical, thrilling next chapter. And the fact that he's willing to give up everything else for a year and a half to get it right tells you exactly how seriously he's taking it.

This isn't a movie. It's a mission.
